newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian ANZ jobs ads fall 1.0 pct in Oct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian ANZ jobs ads fall 1.0 pct in Oct.

text.p: The Australian and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) said on Monday that its job advertisement series fell a seasonally adjusted 1.0 percent in October.
This follows falls of 0.4 percent in September and 2.3 percent in August, leaving the series at its lowest level since January 1994, the bank said.

"The continued gradual decline in job advertising is consistent with other evidence that economic activity remains sluggish," said Saul Eslake, ANZ's chief economist. "There is still as yet no sign of a pick-up in the demand for labour."
The series has now fallen for four consecutive months, the first such sequence since the four months ended December 1991.
Compared with October last year, the number of job ads was down by 12.2 percent.

In trend terms, the number of job advertisements fell by 0.8 percent last month. This represents some improvement over the previous three months, in which job ads have decline at a trend rate of 1.3 percent.
This reflected the fact that the two most recent declines in seasonally adjusted terms have been smaller than the falls recorded earlier in the year, ANZ said.
"Recent trends in job advertising are consistent with net new job creation over the next three months of around 10,000 per month," Eslake said.

"This compares with a requirement of net 20,000 new jobs per month, on average, over the remainder of the 1996/97 financial year if the government's budget forecast of 1.5 percent growth in employment for the year as a whole is to be met," he said.
Job ads fell 12.3 percent in South Australia and 6.2 percent in Tasmania in October following large increases in each case in Sepetmber.
Jobs ads also fell 2.3 percent in New South Wales and 2.6 percent in Queesland.

Increases were recorded in Victoria (3.6 percent), Western Australia (0.8) and Australian Capital Territory (17.0), although the latter followed a 37 percent decline over the first nine months of the year.

ANZ added that the procedure used to derive short-term projections of employment growth from the job advertisement series had been modified in the light of a critique published by the Commonwealth Treasury earlier this year.
